idiom_name: embedded base struct + one struct/query per table (database/sql or sqlx StructScan)
implementation_notes: Go has no inheritance and no ORM mapping to inherit, so the hierarchy dissolves into composition: embed the base struct in each concrete struct (the shared columns appear as fields of the embedded struct), give each concrete type its own table, and let sqlx.StructScan or a hand-written Rows.Scan fill the duplicated columns straight into the embedded fields. Mixed collections come from an explicit UNION ALL query scanned into a row struct with a kind tag, or from separate queries merged behind an interface. The classic structure is not so much replaced as made unnecessary - there is no hierarchy mapping to configure - so choose this mapping deliberately only when leaf-scoped queries dominate and join-free reads matter.
pitfalls: Embedding creates no table relationship: engineers.name and managers.name are separate columns that no compiler check ties together.
A mixed []Employee cannot hold rows from different tables without an interface or a tagged row struct, and the union query must supply the tag and NULL-pad the other subclasses' columns.
Per-table AUTOINCREMENT/serial columns collide across the hierarchy; use one sequence, a UUID column or a shared key table.
